cells.document: Council of Trent, Session VI, Decree on Justification (Waterworth translation, 1848)
cells.section: Chapter V (see also Canons III and IV)
cells.excerpt: neither is man himself utterly without doing anything while he receives that inspiration, forasmuch as he is also able to reject it
cells.shows: Grace comes first and the will cannot move itself to justice without it, yet the person freely assents to and cooperates with that grace and is able to reject it.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (72, synergist-leaning): cooperation and resistibility are defined, while the same chapter and Canon III insist on prevenient grace, which fits a lean short of the pole

cells.document: Council of Trent, Session XIII, Decree concerning the Most Holy Sacrament of the Eucharist (Waterworth translation, 1848)
cells.excerpt: are contained truly, really, and substantially, the body and blood together with the soul and divinity of our Lord Jesus Christ
cells.shows: The canon defines that the whole Christ is substantially present in the Eucharist and anathematises the view that he is there only as in a sign or figure.

cells.document: Second Vatican Council, Dogmatic Constitution on the Church, Lumen Gentium
cells.excerpt: are to be received with thanksgiving and consolation
cells.shows: The Council teaches that the Spirit still distributes charisms, outstanding and simple, among the faithful of every rank, adds that extraordinary gifts are not to be sought after, and reserves judgment of them to the Church's pastors.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (15, continuationist without eager seeking); the same paragraph's caution against seeking extraordinary gifts is why the coordinate sits short of the pole

cells.document: Second Vatican Council, Dogmatic Constitution on the Church, Lumen Gentium
cells.excerpt: calling together a people made up of Jew and gentile, making them one
cells.shows: The Council describes the Church as the new People of God, one people of Jew and Gentile gathered under the new covenant, and calls it the new Israel.

cells.document: Second Vatican Council, Dogmatic Constitution on Divine Revelation, Dei Verbum
cells.excerpt: it is not from Sacred Scripture alone that the Church draws her certainty about everything which has been revealed
cells.shows: The Council teaches that Scripture and sacred tradition form one deposit to be received with the same reverence, and section 10 assigns authentic interpretation to the Church's living teaching office.

cells.document: Council of Trent, Session IV, Decree concerning the Canonical Scriptures (Waterworth translation, 1848)
cells.excerpt: this truth and discipline are contained in the written books, and the unwritten traditions which, received by the Apostles from the mouth of Christ himself
cells.shows: Trent receives the written books and the unwritten apostolic traditions with equal piety and reverence; this is a public-domain text the site may quote where Dei Verbum can only be linked.

cells.document: Second Vatican Council, Constitution on the Sacred Liturgy, Sacrosanctum Concilium
cells.excerpt: the liturgy is the summit toward which the activity of the Church is directed
cells.shows: The Council places the liturgy, centred on the Eucharistic sacrifice, at the summit of the Church's life; section 22 §3 forbids anyone, even a priest, to change it on his own authority, and section 102 sets out the yearly cycle of the Lord's mysteries.

rejected.excerpt: Church has rejected even modified forms of this falsification of the kingdom to come under the name of millenarianism
rejected.shows: The Catechism rejects millenarianism, the expectation that the messianic hope will be realised within history before the final judgment.
rejected.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (8): it excludes the future earthly millennial kingdom that the dispensational pole expects; it does not mention dispensationalism by name
rejected.reason: Document, section and excerpt all check out (CCC 676 on vatican.va, excerpt found verbatim). But the passage rejects millenarianism, and this axis does not turn on the millennium: the site's own summary of the one-people pole includes those who expect a millennial reign on earth. The paragraph says nothing about Israel and the Church being one people or two, so it does not show the Catholic position on THIS axis; it shows amillennial eschatology. Lumen Gentium 9 carries the kingdom cell on its own.

notes: All seven pages were downloaded on 2026-09-19 and every excerpt was checked by script as a verbatim substring of the page text. Trent is quoted from J. Waterworth's 1848 English translation, which is in the public domain (the hosting site's page is a transcription of it); the Vatican II texts and the Catechism are on vatican.va under Libreria Editrice Vaticana copyright, so those cells are marked link_only with excerpts under 20 words. No axis showed a genuine split inside the tradition, so there are no two-sided cells; kingdom and authority each carry a second supporting document, not an opposing one. Eastern Catholic Churches: the ecumenical councils and the Catechism bind the Eastern Catholic Churches as they do the Latin Church, so all cells apply to both; Sacrosanctum Concilium's practical norms are addressed to the Roman rite (SC 3) while its principles apply to all rites. Vatican II's Orientalium Ecclesiarum (1964) and the Code of Canons of the Eastern Churches were not opened in this pass and are therefore not cited. On grace, the coordinate of 72 rather than a pole value is consistent with Trent itself: Session VI chapter V and Canon III require prevenient grace, while Canon IV anathematises the claim that the will 'cannot refuse its consent, if it would'. The Catholic Church also permits both Thomist and Molinist accounts of how grace and freedom relate; no document for that was opened, so nothing is cited for it. Nostra Aetate 4 (opened at https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_decl_19651028_nostra-aetate_en.html, not cited as a cell) uses the phrase 'the new people of God' while adding that the Jews should not be presented as rejected or accursed by God; site copy on the kingdom axis should keep that qualification in view. The table cell cites the Eucharist only; baptism as a means of grace (Trent Session VII) was not opened.
verifier_notes: Independent pass: all seven URLs refetched (HTTP 200) and every excerpt confirmed as a verbatim substring of the page text after whitespace normalisation. Session dates confirmed on the pages themselves (Trent IV 8 April 1546, VI 13 January 1547, XIII 11 October 1551; LG 21 November 1964; DV 18 November 1965; SC 4 December 1963). Side claims checked on the page: Trent VI Canon IV 'cannot refuse its consent, if it would'; LG 9 'the new Israel'; LG 12 'Extraordinary gifts are not to be sought after'; DV 10 on the living teaching office; SC 22 section 3 and SC 102. Wording caution: Trent IV reads 'an equal affection of piety, and reverence', so 'equal piety and reverence' in the shows field is a paraphrase and must not be printed as a quotation. 7 cells verified, 1 rejected; all six axes remain covered.
